name: Northeast Ridge (1963 Route)

rappel_detail.pull: 60m. This first one is described either as a single rope-stretching rappel or split into two shorter ones to the block below.
rappel_detail.notes: Plan on a typical single-rope rappel. Begins the descent of the loose East Ridge crest toward C-J col.
hazards: parties who do not drop far enough below the crest end up committed to loose 4th and low-5th ground and have to climb back up to find the ledge with the cairns
anchors through this descent are mostly slings around large blocks, and some of the wrapped boulders are themselves suspect — check what the sling is attached to, not just the sling
rappel_detail.station: Not on the crest. Traverse the gendarmes on loose ledges roughly 40 to 75 ft below the ridge top, following occasional cairns, until the last two mini-summits come into view, then climb back onto the crest and look down the gully. The first anchors sit beside a small tower on the left side of that gully about 200 ft down, with a cairn on the tower in at least one season.

rappel_detail.pull: Carry spare cord and webbing — some stations are old tat and nothing else. A short rope leaves you between established anchors rather than at them.
hazards: stations are weathered tat and it is normal for the first person down to back one up with gear or add fresh sling
the rappel line is not the climbing line, so retrieving a stuck rope means climbing ground nobody in the party has been on
rappel_detail.station: A big block below the first anchors, where parties who split the opening rope-stretcher into two shorter raps end up.

rappel_detail.notes: A loose gully to climbers' right can be downclimbed instead of rappelled at various points.
hazards: the loose gully to climber's right of the rappels is the downclimbing alternative, and given how rotten the rock is, some parties consider downclimbing the safer of the two
rappel_detail.station: Continuing down the gully toward the heather benches. How many rappels this takes varies with rope length and how much of the loose gully a party is willing to downclimb, so the count between here and the benches is reported as two or three.

hazards: everything here is loose enough that a rappelling party showers the ground below it; take the gully one at a time rather than moving together
the heather feels less secure than the rock steps above it and is very hard to protect, which is the part of this descent accounts single out as genuinely dangerous rather than merely slow
rappel_detail.station: The last of the rappels into the heather benches. From here downclimb the heather to reach the next station.

hazards: aim straight at the col; lines that look more inviting trend away from it and cliff out, forcing a reversal late in the day
rappel_detail.station: A slightly hidden station below the heather benches — look for it before committing to more heather downclimbing, because it is easy to walk past.

rappel_detail.pull: 60m. Counts for the whole ridge vary widely with how much is downclimbed — anywhere from two rappels to eight is reported for the same line.
rappel_detail.notes: Final rappel of the sequence, reaching the Cascade-Johannesburg col.
rappel_detail.anchor: rap-sling anchor, East Ridge crest, above C-J col
hazards: the col sits at the head of the C-J couloir, which is a documented rock and icefall path — do not linger there and do not treat descending it as the easy way out
summit to col alone runs three to five hours, so parties routinely reach this last rappel at dusk with the long traverse out still ahead of them
rappel_detail.station: The final rappel, dropping below the heather benches onto moderately angled slabs directly above the Cascade-Johannesburg col.

descent_text: From the summit, follow the East Ridge — downclimbing/rappelling loose, exposed 3rd/4th-class gendarme ledges (staying well below the crest) — to the Cascade-Johannesburg col. From the col, either rappel the C-J couloir or take the "Doug's Direct" line: traverse beneath the Triplets buttress, sidehill steep heather/meadow slopes, cross the north ridge of Mixup Peak, and descend to Cache Glacier, then follow the Cascade Pass trail back to the trailhead. This descent has taken other parties on Johannesburg's NE-aspect routes on the order of 4.5-9+ hours from the col.
approach: East/Northeast from Cascade Pass trailhead; descend and cross Cascade River, then approach the northeast face via C-J couloir
overview: A more direct, all-rock alternative to the neighboring East Ridge and Northeast Buttress lines: climbs partway up the Cascade-Johannesburg Couloir to a hanging glacier, then follows the leftmost rib to the summit, deliberately avoiding the brush that plagues the other routes.
beta: Grade: 5.7+ YDS, Grade IV, 12 pitches, 4,000 feet. First ascent: 1963. Route: Climb partway up C-J couloir to hanging glacier on right; ascend leftmost rib to summit. Hazards: Objective danger from falling rock/ice, steep snow, exposed scrambling, avalanche potential. Equipment: Small-to-medium alpine rock rack (to 3 inches), 10+ runners, helmet. Best season: July-September. No bush climbing.
gear: small-medium alpine rock rack to 3 inches
ice axe and crampons for the couloir/glacier approach
face: Northeast Face, above the hanging (Sill) glacier
